questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Boundary Conditions?
questions.answer: Boundary conditions give values at the edges of an interval rather than at one starting input. They are common for strings, rods, beams, standing waves, and steady-state fields.

questions.prompt: What does \(x\) mean in Boundary Conditions?
questions.answer: In Boundary Conditions, \(x\) means position along the interval. Its unit is m.

questions.prompt: Identify another important piece of notation used in Boundary Conditions.

questions.prompt: A string mode y(x)=C sin kx plus D cos kx has y(0)=0 and y(L)=0. What restrictions follow?
questions.answer: Apply y(0)=0: \[y(0)=C\sin0+D\cos0=D=0\] Then y(L)=0 gives \[C\sin kL=0\] For a nonzero mode C is not zero, so \[\sin kL=0\] Therefore \[kL=n\pi\] and the allowed modes are set by the boundaries.

questions.prompt: A steady rod has T(x)=C_1x+C_2 with T(0)=T_a and T(L)=T_b. Find C_1 and C_2.
questions.answer: Apply the left boundary: \[T(0)=C_2=T_a\] Apply the right boundary: \[T(L)=C_1L+T_a=T_b\] so \[C_1=\frac{T_b-T_a}{L}\] The temperature profile is \[T(x)=T_a+\frac{T_b-T_a}{L}x\]
